strategyReview: Weekend funding reversion continues to deliver consistent profits across a broad set of assets, while the ONE_TOUCH_HIGH_EDGE_NO shadow is profitable but noisy. The main failures are concentrated in shadow-mined gold touch NO variants (edge fails to predict downside during persistent bullish trends), loose funding reversion signals that trigger outside weekends or without extreme funding, and cross-asset momentum confirmations that do not translate into sufficient spot moves. Several hardcoded-threshold hypotheses (e.g., BTC PM‑IV expansion, absolute funding levels) have broken down as regimes shifted, indicating a need for relative, dynamic conditions.

failureClusters.theme: Gold One-Touch Edge Fails in Uptrends
failureClusters.evidence: Multiple ONE_TOUCH_HIGH_EDGE_NO shadow losses on GOLD where a large underlying-cap edge was present but spot rose sharply (+5.37%, +3.97%), telling us the elevated YES price reflected bullish demand rather than an overpricing error.
failureClusters.recommendation: Add a trend filter to the one-touch NO edge signal (e.g., only short when gold is already below its short-term moving average) so we do not fade a strong uptrend.

failureClusters.theme: Funding Reversion Signals Without Weekend Context
failureClusters.evidence: Several funding reversion hypotheses (CBRS, AAPL, MU) triggered on weekdays when funding was only moderately negative and did not lead to rapid normalization, resulting in sub-50% win rates and flat-to-negative PnL.
failureClusters.recommendation: Restrict these signals to true weekend days (Sat/Sun) and require funding to be in an extreme percentile (e.g., bottom 10% of its 7‑day range) so we only trade true overshoots that reliably revert.

failureClusters.theme: Cross-Asset Momentum Confirmation Fails to Deliver
failureClusters.evidence: The cross_asset_iv_compression_vol_expansion family, which required HYPE above SMA and OI stable as confirmation for BTC longs, posted only a 40% win rate with many small moves that did not surpass +2%.
failureClusters.recommendation: Tighten BTC’s own momentum conditions (e.g., within 2% of the 7‑day high and showing positive daily change) so that HYPE confirmation only adds conviction when the primary asset is already in a strong breakout posture.

newHypotheses.description: Smart‑money fade: when tracked smart wallets are net short YES (smart_flow_stance ≤ -1) on upside one‑touch NO contracts and a sell‑YES edge of at least 3 points exists, enter short (sell YES) expecting spot to decline. In‑sample discovery from FIND‑0020 shows informed flow asymmetry.
newHypotheses.prediction: Spot price of the underlying asset will fall >2% within 7 days as smart money correctly fades overpriced YES demand.

newHypotheses.description: GOLD extreme low put/call ratio short: when gold’s GLD put/call ratio is in the bottom 10% of its 7‑day range (extreme call buying/exhausted puts), short spot regardless of the prevailing trend. Shadow evidence shows +$0.13 PnL on 8 resolved trades (100% WR) despite being blocked by a positive‑trend filter.
newHypotheses.prediction: GOLD spot will decline >2% within 7 days as excessive call positioning unwinds.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑534: only take the gold one‑touch NO short when spot is below the 24h SMA, plus the underlying‑cap edge ≥10 pts. This avoids fading strong uptrends where the cap edge reflects bullish momentum.
newHypotheses.prediction: GOLD spot will decline >2% within 2 days when the edge is large and spot is already in a short‑term downtrend.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑539: restrict CBRS funding reversion to weekends (Sat/Sun) and require funding to be in the extreme low end of its 7‑day distribution (percentile <10). This ensures we only act on true weekend‑driven overshoots that reliably revert.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS perp will rise >2% within 2 days as extreme weekend funding rapidly normalizes into the new trading week.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑537: apply the same weekend‑only filter and deeper extremity condition (funding percentile <10) to AAPL funding reversion. This lifts the win rate from 50% by eliminating weekday triggers where the reversion pattern is unreliable.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL spot will rise >2% within 2 days as deeply negative weekend funding normalizes.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑535: limit MU funding reversion to weekends and require funding to be in its 7‑day bottom decile. This captures the true overshoots that historically produced sharp reversals.
newHypotheses.prediction: MU perp will rise >2% within 2 days as extreme weekend funding rapidly normalizes.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑108: tighten BTC momentum requirements – demand spot be within 2% of its 7‑day high and show a positive 24h change, in addition to HYPE staying above its SMA with stable OI. This ensures we only bet on sustained, strong BTC breakouts.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will rise >2% within 7 days when strong primary momentum is confirmed by HYPE risk‑on participation.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑001: replace absolute PM‑IV thresholds with a regime‑relative condition – PM IV z‑score below –1.5 on a 30‑day window, indicating extreme compression versus its own recent history. This should capture dislocations regardless of the absolute level of IV.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will make a >2% absolute move within 3 days as the compressed prediction‑market IV snaps back.

hypothesisReviews.observation: All recent test outcomes were losses where GOLD spot rose when the underlying‑cap edge was large. The edge did not signal overpriced YES but rather persistent bullish demand that pushed spot higher.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying‑cap edge on gold upside touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Half of tests failed because CBRS funding < –10% either stayed negative or overshot further without causing the required spot move within 2 days, indicating the reversion timeframe was too tight.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: CBRS funding < –10% reliably normalizes within 2 days leading to a >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The signal triggered many weekday events where funding was only mildly negative and did not revert quickly, producing losses. The pattern worked only on weekends with severely stretched funding.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: AAPL funding below –10% on any day rapidly normalizes and yields a >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Despite HYPE remaining above SMA and OI stable, BTC often failed to clear the +2% hurdle within 7 days, suggesting the cross‑asset confirmation did not add sufficient predictive power.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE spot above SMA with stable OI confirms a >2% BTC long move within 7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Most tests showed MU funding < –10% without a corresponding >2% spot rally within 2 days; instead spot often drifted or declined further.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: MU funding below –10% rapidly normalizes and causes a >2% spot rally within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The absolute IV thresholds (PM IV <46, opt IV >49) are no longer effective in the current lower‑IV environment; many triggers produced sub‑2% spot moves, indicating the regime has shifted.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: PM IV underpricing options IV by >8% reliably leads to a >2% absolute spot move within 3 days.

journalEntry: Tonight’s review focused on the persistent underperformance of several shadow‑mined and early hypothesis variants. Gold one‑touch NO edge fails because elevated YES prices in a bull market are not a mispricing but a reflection of real demand — we must add trend filters. Weekend funding reversion hypotheses (CBRS, AAPL, MU) work well only when they are restricted to actual weekends and extreme funding percentiles; loose triggers on weekdays erode performance. The cross‑asset momentum family needs tighter primary momentum conditions so that HYPE’s confirmation is applied only to already strong BTC breakouts. BTC PM‑IV expansion must move from absolute thresholds to regime‑relative z‑scores to adapt to changing volatility. New hypotheses from FIND‑0020 (smart‑flow fade) and FIND‑0053 (extreme GLD PC ratio short) are added based on robust shadow discovery statistics and will enter shadow‑test queues.
